subjectLine: Keep Your Winter Garden Healthy in Portland
previewText: Protect perennials, care for ferns, and make the most of the quiet season.

contentBlocks.tagline: Winter garden care tips for a thriving spring

contentBlocks.imageAlt: Lush flower beds and manicured shrubs in The Butchart Gardens in Victoria, Canada

contentBlocks.body:
This is the perfect time to give your garden a little extra attention before spring arrives. Even while most plants are dormant, a few simple steps now will set the stage for healthier, more vibrant growth later.

Focus on protecting vulnerable perennials and maintaining your garden tools. Winter is also ideal for planning any changes or additions you want to make come spring.

contentBlocks.headline: Winter Care for Ferns and Perennials
contentBlocks.body: Portland’s cool, wet winters are ideal for Christmas Ferns. Check that your ferns and other evergreens are not getting waterlogged by clearing away fallen leaves and ensuring good drainage. For perennials like Black-Eyed Susan, trim back old stems but leave some foliage for added winter protection and to provide habitat for beneficial insects. Regularly check for signs of rot or frost damage and remove affected plant material promptly.
